subject: ProtonLane: high-latency surge postmortem and exec action cadence
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@protonlane.com>
To: naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben.ortiz@protonlane.com
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in API latency from 06/12 08:55 — urgent

Naomi —

We saw a large latency spike across our production calls to the Redwood embeddings route starting ~08:55 PDT and lasting ~20 minutes. 99th percentile went from ~380ms to ~1.6s; error rate on a subset of requests reached 4.2%. Our customers reported dropped responses during checkout. This is causing a major customer-visible impact for ProtonLane.

Can your team share any immediate findings and an ETA for root cause / mitigation? Ben (CC) is leading ops on our side; procurement and execs are asking for an RCA and corrective plan.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform, ProtonLane
attachments: protonlane-incident-timeline.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

From: naomi.feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@protonlane.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in API latency from 06/12 08:55 — urgent

Aisha — thanks for the heads up and the timeline PDF. I’ve opened an incident and looped our on-call (Jonas) and SRE (Karthik). Preliminary blameless snapshot: we observed a KV-cache pressure event in the embeddings serving pool which increased backend tokenization latency and forced fallbacks to a slower decode path. We have an active mitigation (short-term cache tuning + temporary routing to a higher-throughput model variant) in place; I'll confirm once the metrics have fully normalized.

Immediate asks from us: can you share the ProtonLane traffic profile for the window (sample request IDs) and any alert thresholds you use? That will help validate our replay.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Spike in API latency from 06/12 08:55 — urgent

Aisha / Naomi — brief status update:

- Root cause (initial): a KV cache eviction storm triggered by a traffic pattern with many large-prefix requests; that caused repeated recomputation of tokenization state and forced requests into a fallback decode path with higher CPU usage.
- Impact window: 08:55–09:15 PDT, matching your timeline (validated against edge telemetry).
- Temporary mitigations applied (08:58–09:06): raised cache size for the affected pool, adjusted eviction thresholds, and traffic-steered 12% of ProtonLane traffic to a higher-throughput variant.
- Current status: P95 back to baseline, P99 trending down but still slightly elevated (1.0s).

Next steps: Karthik will coordinate a deep-dive and produce an RCA packet by Friday 06/16. Naomi — recommend we schedule an executive readout with ProtonLane for early next week and share an actionable remedial plan (config + long-term runtime safeguards).

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in API latency from 06/12 08:55 — urgent

Aisha / team — attaching the draft RCA and recommended corrective actions. Summary highlights:

- Cause: workload skew + insufficient KV cache headroom for large-prefix fanout. Under that workload, tokenization hot paths were re-invoked frequently.
- Fixes proposed:
  1) Short-term (1–2 days): permanent increase to cache headroom for ProtonLane’s serving pool; automated eviction smoothing to prevent micro-storms; apply canary traffic steer to validate.
  2) Medium-term (2–4 weeks): runtime change to pre-compute prefix-shared tokenization state and add stress tests for high-fanout patterns.
  3) Long-term (quarter): model-routing policy to detect and throttle high-cost prefixes and provide transparent billing guardrails.
- Customer impact & compensation: propose a one-time credit (2 weeks of average usage) while we complete mitigations; legal/procurement can finalize.

Attached: rca-draft-protonlane.docx (RCA + timeline + action matrix).

Planned deliverables: final RCA doc (06/16), exec readout proposal (06/18), mitigation rollout (canary 06/14, full 06/20).

Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference
attachments: rca-draft-protonlane.docx (docx, 240KB)

Aisha / Ben — thanks again for the partnership this week. Quick recap from our exec readout this morning and the action tracker we agreed on (finals linked):

- RCA: confirmed root cause and the timeline (see Drive packet).
- Immediate (done): canary (06/14) validated reduced P99; cache headroom increased for the ProtonLane serving pool.
- Short-term (in progress, target 06/22): eviction smoothing rollout and automated alerting for early cache-pressure signals. Owner: Jonas.
- Medium-term (in design, target 07/09): prefix-sharing tokenization precompute and stress harness. Owner: Karthik.
- Customer remediation: agreed credit mechanism — Redwood will send a credit memo for the impacted window by 06/21. Owner: Kimberly (finance liaison).
- Exec follow-up cadence: weekly check-ins for two weeks; then monthly health reports for the quarter.

Action tracker links: https://drive.redwood/protonlane/rca-final, HubSpot PLN-5832 timeline and tasks: https://hubspot.company/contacts/PLN-5832. Attachments pushed to shared Drive (protonlane-incident-timeline.pdf, rca-draft-protonlane.docx).

Please reply if any item is missing; otherwise we’ll mark the incident as mitigated and keep the action tracker open until all items close.
